# Test Fixtures

## `test_440hz_1s_16k.wav`

- **Format**: 16-bit PCM WAV, mono
- **Sample rate**: 16000 Hz
- **Duration**: 1 second
- **Content**: 440 Hz sine wave (A4 concert pitch) at -6 dBFS
- **Purpose**: Used by audio processing tests (recording, transcription, resampling)
- **Generated by**: `generate_fixture.py` (deterministic — same input produces same output)

## Python helper modules

The `tests/fixtures/` package hosts shared factory helpers that were
previously copy-pasted across the test tree. Each module owns the
SINGLE canonical version of one factory; test files migrate from
their inline helpers to the canonical import over time (see the
"Migration status" section in each module's docstring).

- `app_helpers.py` — `make_voice_typer_app` (real `VoiceTyperApp` with
  hardware/GUI deps mocked), `make_sine` (float32 numpy sine wave),
  `join_model_load_thread` (best-effort join of `app.models.
  _model_load_thread` after a test, mirroring the teardown in
  `tests/app/conftest.py:59-61`).
- `ipc_test_helpers.py` — DI-mode fakes for `IPCServer`:
  `make_fake_app`, `make_fake_service`, `make_ipc_server_with_fakes`.
- `sidecar_ws_test_helpers.py` — `_make_fake_server` for sidecar WS
  tests.
- `recorder_test_helpers.py` — `make_recorder()` consolidates the 2
  byte-for-byte copies of the secure-clear path's `_make_recorder` in
  `tests/test_secure_clear_no_resample_segments.py` and
  `tests/test_secure_clear_array.py`.

## Removed fixtures (XS-43)

The following fixtures were removed in session XS (finding XS-43) because
they were never referenced by any test code (verified via
`rg -n 'silence\.wav|tone\.wav|noise\.wav' tests/` → zero matches) and
`tone.wav` was a byte-for-byte duplicate of `test_440hz_1s_16k.wav`
(identical sha256):

- `silence.wav` — aspirational VAD/silence-detection fixture; the tests
  were never written.
- `tone.wav` — duplicate of `test_440hz_1s_16k.wav` (same content,
  different filename).
- `noise.wav` — aspirational noise-floor fixture; no test loads it.

Only `test_440hz_1s_16k.wav` is retained on disk. The `wav_fixture_path`
pytest fixture that previously returned its path was removed in RT-16
(no test imported it — tests that need the WAV construct the path inline).

## Removed factory helpers (TK-25)

The following canonical factory modules were removed in TK-25 because
no test ever imported them (verified via `rg 'clipboard_test_helpers|'
'shutdown_test_helpers' tests/` → zero matches outside the definition
files — the docstrings were written aspirationally when the modules were
created, but the inline helpers in the test files were never migrated):

- `clipboard_test_helpers.py` — `make_clipboard_manager(**overrides)` /
  `make_clipboard_snapshot(...)`; the 5 inline `_make_cm` / `_make_snapshot`
  copies in `tests/test_clipboard*.py` remain inline.
- `shutdown_test_helpers.py` — `make_fake_shutdown_app(**overrides)`;
  the 13 inline `_FakeApp` copies in `tests/test_shutdown_*.py` /
  `tests/test_app_cleanup.py` / `tests/test_ipc_send_shutdown_allowlist.py`
  remain inline.

## Removed factory helpers (RT-16)

The following factory helpers in `tests/fixtures/ipc_test_helpers.py`
were removed in RT-16 because no test imported them (verified via
`rg -n 'make_fake_sidecar_ws_server|make_fake_recorder' tests/` →
matches only in the definition file and `tests/fixtures/README.md`):

- `make_fake_sidecar_ws_server` — aspirational XS-42 migration target;
  the sidecar WS tests continue to use their inline `_make_fake_server`
  helpers, so the canonical factory was never wired up. (Sidecar WS
  tests were later consolidated via `sidecar_ws_test_helpers.py`
  instead — see above.)
- `make_fake_recorder` — same: aspirational XS-42 migration target; the
  recorder tests continue to use their inline `_make_recorder` helpers.
  (The two byte-for-byte copies were later consolidated via
  `recorder_test_helpers.py` — see above.)

The retained exports (`make_fake_app`, `make_fake_service`,
`make_ipc_server_with_fakes`) are actively used by `tests/handlers/*`
(`tests/handlers/conftest.py` imports `make_fake_app` and
`make_fake_service` to back its `fake_app` / `fake_service` fixtures)
and by the top-level `tests/test_ipc_server.py`,
`tests/test_di_providers.py`, `tests/test_security_fixes.py`,
`tests/test_keyboard_ownership_watchdog.py`,
`tests/test_tcp_dispatch_concurrency.py`, `tests/test_cursor_pagination.py`,
`tests/test_onboarding_permissions.py`, `tests/test_config_sanitizer.py`,
`tests/test_heartbeat*.py`, `tests/test_sidecar_ready_emitted.py`,
`tests/test_sidecar_ws_ready_ordering.py`,
`tests/test_tcp_idle_read_timeout.py` files. The previously documented
claim that `tests/server/*` imports them was inaccurate —
`rg 'make_fake_app|make_fake_service|make_ipc_server_with_fakes'
tests/server/` returns zero matches (verified 2026-08-03).
